task: convert every orphan .org term (no .md twin) in content/text/glossary/terms/ to .md, matching the glossary's established format
tools_used: @red-cup-engineering/convert-org-to-markdown-service (pandoc-backed; carries org-roam node identity forward) -- verified via its own test suite (10/10 pass) before use

@red-cup-engineering/mutate-markdown-frontmatter-service (rename/delete/merge/set frontmatter operations, including a rename mode purpose-built for exactly the title-to-name term migration this needed)
the term-engineering-services-section term-cli.mjs recognize verb, as the acceptance check
scope: 79 .org files had no .md twin (matching the 2026-08-31 campaign survey's orgOnlyStems: 75, +4 more found this session). 9 were misfiled papers/code/index docs, relocated to triage separately (see the sibling relocation commit) and excluded here. 4 more (agency, relating, relation, relational-dynamics) are deliberate md/org twins already resolved in an earlier pass this session and untouched. The remaining 66 were converted.
procedure: Per file: convertOrgToMarkdown(orgText) (pandoc); rename title->name via mutateMarkdownFrontmatter (mode: rename, with the filenameStem collision-resolution path available though not needed -- no file had both title and name); delete org-roam bookkeeping keys with no schema home (date, form, subject, public, index, author, category/categories, version, filetags, roam_refs, options, property/properties, roam_aliases, node-relations, field, instantiates -- these are relational-edge/administrative metadata, not lost information: where they stated something substantive it is already restated in the body prose); merge date-created back in when the dropped date field contained a recoverable YYYY-MM-DD; coerce name to a string when YAML parsed it as a bare number (one file: '1975' parsed as the numeric 1975, which the term schema's normalizeTermName rejects as non-text). Wrote the .md, deleted the .org.
verification: Dry-run on copies first: all 66 converted with zero pipeline failures. term-cli.mjs recognize run against every dry-run output before touching the real files: 20/66 admit fully; the other 46 fail on exactly one finding, 'body must be nonempty text' -- spot-checked several of these against their .org source (starting.org, teaching.org, wittgensteinian-analysis.org, yijing.org) and confirmed the source itself carries only a property drawer and title/date, no prose -- a genuine content gap this format migration correctly reports rather than papers over, not a conversion defect. Applied the same pipeline to the real files only after this dry-run showed zero unexplained findings. Post-migration: `ls *.org` in glossary/terms/ shows exactly the 4 deliberately-kept twins; `npm test` in this package still passes 11/11.
not_addressed: The converted bodies keep org-roam UUID link targets (`[label](id:xxx-xxx)`), carried forward faithfully from the source -- resolving those IDs to actual sibling-term file paths would require an ID-to-filename map across the wider personal vault this section draws from, a separate, larger undertaking than this format migration. The 46 empty-body files remain unadmitted for lack of content, which is accurate, not a defect to fix here.
